Vioxx, the painkiller pulled from the market in 2004, is the cautionary tale at the heart of this Joe Rogan Experience segment. Merck sold the drug for arthritis pain before studies linked it to heart attacks and strokes. Tens of thousands of lawsuits followed the recall.

Rogan and his guest walk through what the company knew and when it knew it. They discuss how drug trials can hide risks and how regulators missed the signals. The talk widens into trust in big drug firms as a whole. It is pharma's warning story, told straight for the wary.
podcast-tuckercarlson-DDD_N6ZcCV4:
Alex Jones, the broadcaster behind InfoWars, joins Tucker Carlson to warn of what he calls a globalist death cult driving the world toward civil war and the rise of the Antichrist. The conversation is apocalyptic in the literal sense: Jones frames current politics as the visible edge of a spiritual end-times conflict.

Carlson, who has defended Jones as a truth-teller about power, gives him room to build the whole picture. Jones mixes news items, documents he cites, and prophecy into one urgent narrative. His claims are famously contested and have cost him dearly in court; the episode preserves his current presentation anyway. For listeners, it documents how the two most polarizing voices in American media sound in conversation, and what their large audiences are being told to expect.
podcast-tuckercarlson-DWybONUddV4:
Podcaster Chris Williamson, host of Modern Wisdom, joins Tucker Carlson with a guide to being happy. Williamson built his show around interviews on life, meaning, and self-improvement. Here he also takes on feminist claims he says sabotage men's lives.

Williamson shares habits and mindsets he credits for a calmer, stronger life. He and Carlson debate what modern advice gets wrong about men, work, and love. The talk mixes practical steps with cultural argument. Seekers get straight talk on the good life from a man who has interviewed hundreds about it.
podcast-tuckercarlson-H1v7qwoCVV4:
Buckley Carlson, the host's son and a former Trump speechwriter, joins Tucker Carlson for a family affair of an episode. Buckley shares tales from writing the president's speeches and reveals Trump's pointed texts to Representative Marjorie Taylor Greene. The Epstein cover-up also gets the family's treatment.

The younger Carlson explains how a Trump speech comes together under deadline pressure. Father and son trade views on the movement's fights and its future. Carlson asks what the texts reveal about Trump's style of rule. Political and curious viewers get insider tales told across a dinner-table divide of generations.
podcast-tuckercarlson-LT6kEK02_V4:
Journalist Glenn Greenwald talks with Tucker Carlson about leaks, Brazil, and shared views. Greenwald helped publish the Snowden files and later built a career in Brazil. The episode title names Julian Assange and Edward Snowden.

The two men note how often they reach the same view from different paths. They talk about loyalty, honesty, and how beliefs form early. Greenwald then turns to Brazil and its court fights over speech. Listeners hear a wide talk that ties whistleblowers, exile, and free speech into one thread. Both men present candor as a duty, not a brand.
